clinician.trajectory_summary: An 18-year-old girl presented with a ten-year history of recurrent left migrainous headaches associated with ipsilateral intermittent oculomotor nerve palsy. A Brain MRI with contrast revealed an enhancing nodule on the cisternal segment of the left oculomotor nerve, suggestive of schwannoma. On follow-up, she no longer presented additional episodes.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with recurrent left migrainous headaches and ipsilateral intermittent oculomotor nerve palsy.
Brain MRI revealed an enhancing nodule on the cisternal segment of the left oculomotor nerve suggestive of schwannoma.
On follow-up, the patient no longer presented additional episodes.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: The MRI finding of an enhancing nodule on the oculomotor nerve specifically suggestive of schwannoma makes other etiologies less likely.
